entries.proposition: Two patients with missense CACNA1G variants and infantile-onset DEE-type presentations. Case 1 (L909F, gain of function) had refractory seizures with regression and ataxia and was seizure free for two years on single-drug treatment at age 9 (Results 2.1); case 2 (L208P, mixed) had myoclonic jerks from 4 months and stopped medication at 4 years after a few years without observable spells, yet is the more severely affected child overall. Seizure burden did not track the severity of the biophysical defect, and the case descriptions carry no antiseizure-drug response data bearing on T-type block.
entries.snippet: Anti-seizure medication (ASM) was discontinued at 4 years of age after a few years of no observable spells.
entries.anchor: Results 2.1, case 2 description (case 1 course in the same subsection)

entries.proposition: L909F is described as a gain of function (hyperpolarising shift of activation by about 4.5 mV, slower deactivation); L208P as mixed gain and loss (activation and inactivation shifted hyperpolarised, slow inactivation and deactivation, slow recovery from inactivation, reduced availability at repetitive stimulation). The authors infer clinical severity correlates with functional severity, from two patients.
entries.snippet: Our electrophysiological data are congruent with the clinical findings of a milder phenotype for the L909F patient versus the L208P (Table 1).

entries.proposition: The authors state that Cacna1g knockout mice are less prone to absence epilepsy, and that Cacna1g levels act as a genetic modifier in two other seizure models (higher levels increase spontaneous seizures in an Scn2a model, lower levels reduce them in a Dravet-type model, with better survival), proposing Cav3.1 as a possible target in SCN1A and SCN2A epilepsy. All of this is cited, not measured here.
entries.snippet: Similarly, in a mouse model of Dravet syndrome due to Scn1a mutation, decreased Cacna1g expression results in a partial amelioration of disease phenotypes with improved survival and reduced spontaneous seizure frequency [37].

entries.proposition: A statement of what the electrophysiology cannot yet say about neurons: the full-scale neuron-level consequences of the variants are unknown, the authors speculate L208P could not support burst firing because of low availability at high stimulation rate, and propose dynamic-clamp work. So the gain-of-function label rests on HEK-cell current properties, not on neuronal firing.
entries.snippet: Clearly, more work remains to be done in order to fully understand the neuron-scale mechanisms caused by pathogenic Cav3.1 variants.

entries.proposition: Cav3.1 expression is present at birth, region- and age-dependent and rises through postnatal development; isoform b is the fetal isoform and longer splice variants predominate in the adult brain. The channel in a preweaning animal is therefore of a different splice composition from the adult one.
entries.snippet: Isoform b is normally found in the fetal brain, whereas the transcripts of the longer splice variants predominate in the adult brain [30].

entries.proposition: Figure 1 read as an image: peak current density in heterologous cells is larger than wild type for two variants (about minus 260 against minus 205 pA/pF, at minus 25 to minus 30 mV) and similar to wild type for L208P (about minus 175 against minus 205); half-activation voltage is shifted hyperpolarised for all three (steady-state activation curves left of wild type: M1508V furthest, then L208P, then L909F); the steady-state inactivation curves of L208P and M1508V sit left of wild type and L909F close to it.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1D-F: peak density L909F and M1508V about -260 vs WT about -205 pA/pF; L208P about -175; activation curves all left of WT (M1508V > L208P > L909F); inactivation L208P and M1508V left of WT, L909F close.

entries.proposition: Figure 2 read as an image: the deactivation time constant is much slower for L208P (about 80 ms at minus 50 mV against about 6 ms for wild type) and M1508V (about 46 ms), slightly slower for L909F (about 11 ms); the activation time constant is slower for L208P (about 25 ms at minus 55 mV against about 7 ms) and M1508V (about 17 ms); the inactivation time constant is much slower for L208P (about 225 ms at minus 50 mV against about 135 ms) and M1508V stays near 40 ms at depolarised potentials against about 12 ms for wild type and L909F.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2B-D: deactivation tau at -50 mV: L208P about 80, M1508V about 46, L909F about 11, WT about 6 ms; activation tau L208P about 25, M1508V about 17 vs WT about 7; inactivation tau L208P about 225 vs WT about 135 at -50 mV.

entries.proposition: Figure 3 read as an image: recovery from inactivation is much slower for L208P (about 65 percent recovered at 1000 ms and about 91 percent at 8000 ms against full recovery near 1000 ms for wild type), modestly slower for M1508V at short intervals and not different for L909F.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3B: L208P about 65% recovered at 1000 ms, about 91% at 8000 ms; WT full by about 1000 ms; M1508V slightly slower at short intervals; L909F like WT.

entries.proposition: Figure 4 read as an image: with repeated depolarisation at 1 Hz the current falls to about 32 percent (L208P) and about 48 percent (M1508V) of the first pulse against about 85 percent for wild type and about 80 percent for L909F; at 3 Hz the plateau is about 12 percent (L208P), 20 percent (M1508V), 37 percent (L909F) and 62 percent (wild type).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4B: 1 Hz plateau L208P about 32%, M1508V about 48%, WT about 85%, L909F about 80%; 3 Hz L208P about 12%, M1508V about 20%, L909F about 37%, WT about 62%.
